MicroSD socket and flash LED already on board
Use external 5V supply through board 5V input

chips_on_reference_schematic.role: image buffer; exact chip/capacity depends on physical board

blockers: Bare OV2640 flex is not a USB camera. Needs matching controller, supply rails, clock and driver.
ESP32-S3 camera clones are a different pin map despite a similar shape.
GPIO0 also carries camera XCLK: release the flashing jumper before running.
A regulator supplying 5V does not make ESP32 UART pins 5V tolerant.
Cannot promise outdoor/weatherproof/security-appliance reliability from this devboard.
donors.availability: Candidate from abandoned maker/3D-printer camera projects or used modules; no claim that a random consumer camera contains this board.

donors.title: Raspberry Pi Camera Module 2 / IMX219

identity.pcb_revision: Not established from manufacturer text; record the actual board silkscreen and do not equate product version 2 with a specific PCB revision

recoverable: Camera module, lens and intact ribbon cable as a unit
donors.compatibility: Raspberry Pi board with supported CSI connector. Pi 4 and earlier flagship boards use 15-to-15 cable; Pi 5 and Pi Zero use standard-to-mini 15-to-22 cable.
startup: With Pi powered off, seat the correct camera ribbon and latch both ends.
Boot Raspberry Pi OS with current camera software.
Run rpicam-hello --list-cameras; require IMX219 to appear.
Run rpicam-still --output test.jpg; open the actual image.
blockers: Not USB; passive ribbon-to-USB cables cannot provide the needed CSI receiver/driver.
A loose sensor from a phone is not automatically Camera Module 2 even when its sensor is IMX219.
Standard camera filters infrared; NoIR is a distinct variant, and darkness needs appropriate illumination.

wiring.note: Board supply input, not a GPIO
Only while resetting into upload mode; remove before running

configuration: Install/select esp32 by Espressif Systems 3.3.12; open the example supplied by the same installed version.
Select the AI Thinker ESP32-CAM board definition where available.
In board_config.h comment out CAMERA_MODEL_ESP_EYE and enable only CAMERA_MODEL_AI_THINKER.
Set ssid and password in CameraWebServer.ino locally; never publish credentials.
Provide at least 3MB application partition as required by the example.

steps.title: Identify the board
steps.action: Match camera connector, ESP32-S module and actual header labels against the photo. Keep OV2640 seated.
steps.pass: The physical board matches AI-Thinker pin map.

steps.title: Connect power and serial
steps.action: Power off before wiring. Connect common ground and crossed UART; use 3.3V UART signals and 5V board power.
steps.pass: No 5V signal is connected to U0R; camera flex is aligned.

steps.title: Upload
steps.action: Hold GPIO0 at GND, reset, upload the correctly configured Espressif example.
steps.pass: Upload succeeds; no repeated brownout messages.

steps.title: Start normally
steps.action: Remove GPIO0–GND link and reset. Open serial monitor at 115200 baud.
steps.pass: Camera initialization succeeds, Wi-Fi connects and a local http:// address is printed.

steps.title: Get a real frame
steps.action: Open that address on the same LAN. Start stream and capture a still.
steps.pass: Motion updates in the live view; still image is nonblank and correctly oriented.

steps.title: Make it useful
steps.action: Put board in an insulated case with cable strain relief and a clear lens. Run a 30-minute local stream, then power-cycle and reconnect.
steps.pass: ARC proposed acceptance test: no resets, reconnect succeeds, no exposed live contacts. Not yet a certified unattended alarm.

troubleshoot.check: GPIO0 low during reset; adapter TX→U0R and RX→U0T; actual serial port.
Correct AI_THINKER switch, matching sensor, seated ribbon and stable power.
Supply and cable voltage drop; do not mask by disabling brownout detection.

troubleshoot.symptom: Page opens but camera does not run after flashing
troubleshoot.check: Remove GPIO0–GND jumper, reset and verify camera log.

limitations: Stock example is a local HTTP prototype; no claim of authentication, encrypted remote access, recording or motion alarms.
Do not expose this unmodified example directly to the internet.
First qualify camera and power before adding PIR, recording or an alarm output.
